value: tax.compute_tax(region, lines, discount_pct) -> int. region: customer region code str (e.g. "TX", "NY", "OR") or null for an unknown customer. lines: list of {"category": str, "amount_cents": int} for ALL line items of the order (tax.py itself drops exempt categories). discount_pct: number, percent (10 means 10%), 0 if none. Returns int cents: tax amount, rounded half up to the cent. Raises KeyError if region is a non-null code not in rates.csv.
why: Team convention: money in int cents, percent as percent numbers, missing lookup raises KeyError. tax.py owns exempt-category and discount logic, so it needs the line categories and the discount. Returning only the tax amount keeps invoice.py from computing tax rules.

value: region=null (unknown customer) -> tax 0 cents. Region code not in rates.csv -> KeyError.
why: data_tax/RULES.md says an unknown customer pays 0% tax, but the team convention says a failed lookup raises KeyError. Reconciled: the 0% rule applies when the customer is unknown and pricing passes null; a region code that is present but has no rate is a data error and raises KeyError.

value: decimal.Decimal dollars, quantized to 0.01 with ROUND_HALF_UP where rounding is needed
why: Team coding standard: money is Decimal('12.50') in dollars.

value: multiplier as Decimal: 10% off -> 0.90; 8.25% tax -> 1.0825; no discount or no tax -> 1.0000
why: Team standard: percentages are multipliers. For multipliers the not-found default is 1.0000 (no discount / no tax), not 0, because 0 would mean 100% off.
Superseded: team already proposed int cents (TAX_API) and float dollars (PRICING_API). I follow the proposed team conventions rather than my own Decimal standard, to avoid a mismatch at integration.
Superseded: team uses percent numbers / fractions (PRICING_API, TAX_API). Following those.

Conflicts with the team standard: (1) price is float dollars; team standard is int cents (e.g. 1250 = $12.50). (2) discount is a fraction (0.10); team standard is percent numbers (10). (3) get_item/get_customer return None on a miss; team standard is KeyError. Suggested v2: price_cents int, discount_pct number (percent), and KeyError on a miss. For the customer-unknown case, the tax layer takes region=null (see UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER_TAX), so pricing can still return region null only if the customer record exists but has no region; otherwise raise KeyError.

value: tax.tax_percent(region) -> float: the sales tax rate in percent for the region (8.25 means 8.25%); region None (unknown customer) or no rate -> 0; KeyError for a region code not in rates.csv, same as compute_tax
why: The spec requires the tax percent shown on the invoice to come from tax.py. compute_tax returns only cents, so this additional function supplies the percent. Same region input, so invoice.py never does rate logic.

Conflicts with UNKNOWN_CUSTOMER_TAX: 'unknown -> 0' is only right for region=null. A non-null region code not in rates.csv must raise KeyError. Fix the wording to: tax_percent(region) -> percent number (8.25 = 8.25%); region=null -> 0; region code not in rates.csv -> KeyError. I accept the function name and signature.

Accept as written (float dollars, discount fraction). Units are converted to int cents at the invoice boundary, which tax.py does not handle. The miss behaviour is None as in v1; invoice catches it either way.
Superseded by v2 (discount as fraction; money as int cents at the tax boundary).
